title: Meeting Wingy Manone in Albuquerque and moving to New Orleans
summary: He met Wingy while with Doc Ross around 1923, worked together, and Wingy sent for him to come to New Orleans and Biloxi in 1925.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And Boots and his buddies, too, over there in the thirties. I guess that was a good swing band. Uh-huh. Um, when did you first meet Wingy?

Well, I was with Doc Bross, and we were working out of Albuquerque, New Mexico. And he came through there, and, uh, you know, the trains used to stop for lunch in Albuquerque. And I was living in a hotel right across from the station, and he heard, he'd heard about me. So, during this 30-minute lunch period, he came over to the hotel and looked me up. And this was, uh, about 1923 or something like that. And he was on his way out to join a fellow in Phoenix by the name of Ham Crawford. So I said, well, if you get out there and you don't find everything to your liking, and you want to make a change, well, I can swing it with Doc Bross if he'd come back and join us. And he did. So we worked together quite a while. That was 1925 when he came back to work with us. That's the last when I worked with him. And I came to New Orleans. He sent for me to come down here to New Orleans and Biloxi, along about 1925. I actually left Doc Bross, and he came down here by himself.
